{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMmFNZj1bU1CVyYEu9Bu","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT ARCHITECTURE.md ===\n# ARCHITECTURE: Quakes\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Module layout, boundaries and technical decisions for the `quakes` earthquake feed reporter command-line tool. |\n| Depends On  | None |\n| Provides    | quakes executable, cli.main, cli.testing.cli_runner, cli.errors.UsageError, cli.errors.OperationalFailure |\n| Consumes    | None |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes` is a Python 3.11+ standard-library command-line tool. `quakes fetch` saves a period of the\nUSGS FDSN event feed as a GeoJSON file. Five report commands (`summary`, `top`, `daily`, `regions`,\n`near`) read a saved file and write a CSV report to standard output. Every report value is computed\nfrom the file being read; nothing is embedded.\n\n## Technology Stack\n\nDerived from `TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md`, which remains the decision of record.\n\n| Technology | Where it applies |\n|---|---|\n| Python 3.11+ (standard library only) | All application code: `cli/` package and the `quakes` executable. |\n| CLI (`cli.md`) | The `quakes` entry point and the `cli` package with `main(argv) -> int`. |\n| pytest | The project test suite under `tests/`, run through `bin/test.sh`. |\n| USGS GeoJSON | Input format for every report; fetched with `urllib.request`. |\n| POSIX sh | `bin/test.sh` and the supplied grader `sources/run.sh`. |\n\n## Module Layout\n\nAll application code lives in the `cli` package at the application root.\n\n| Module | Responsibility | Built by story |\n|---|---|---|\n| `quakes` (root, executable) | `#!` Python launcher that calls `cli.main` and exits with its return value | foundation |\n| `cli/__init__.py` | `main(argv) -> int`: help check, parse, dispatch, exit-code mapping, writing stdout | foundation, then feature stories |\n| `cli/testing.py` | `cli_runner(*args) -> (exit_code, stdout, stderr)` | foundation |\n| `cli/errors.py` | `UsageError` and `OperationalFailure`, both `Exception` subclasses | foundation |\n| `cli/options.py` | `COMMANDS`, `Invocation`, `parse_args(argv)` | feature-cli-dispatch |\n| `cli/commands.py` | `HANDLERS` registry and `dispatch(invocation) -> str` | feature-cli-dispatch |\n| `cli/help.py` | `wants_help(argv)`, `help_text(command)` | feature-help |\n| `cli/reader.py` | `Event`, `read_events(path)` | feature-feed-reader |\n| `cli/normalise.py` | `format_time`, `region_of`, number formatting helpers | feature-event-normalise |\n| `cli/filtering.py` | `filter_min_mag(events, m)` | feature-min-mag |\n| `cli/reports.py` and per-report modules | One compute function and one format function per report | report stories |\n| `cli/fetch.py` | `http_get(url)` and the fetch handler | feature-fetch |\n\nReading the file, filtering, computing each report, and formatting are separate functions, each\nunit-tested on its own.\n\n## Control Flow\n\n`main(argv)` runs, in order:\n\n1. Reconfigure standard output to UTF-8 with `\\n` newlines when the stream supports it.\n2. If `cli.help.wants_help(argv)`, write the help text to standard output and return `0`.\n3. `invocation = parse_args(argv)`, then `text = commands.dispatch(invocation)`.\n4. Write `text` to standard output once, only after the handler has returned, and return `0`.\n5. `UsageError` returns `2` and `OperationalFailure` returns `1`. Each writes exactly one diagnostic\n   line to standard error and nothing to standard output.\n\nA handler is a function `handler(invocation) -> str` returning the complete standard-output text. A\nhandler never writes to standard output itself. This is what guarantees that a failing command\nwrites nothing to standard output.\n\n## Boundaries and Ownership\n\n| Boundary | Owning module | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Local file reads | `cli/reader.py` | The only module that opens a feed file for reading. |\n| Network | `cli/fetch.py` `http_get` | The only module that opens a connection; tests replace `http_get`. |\n| Standard output | `cli/__init__.py` `main` | Handlers return text. |\n| Standard error | `cli/__init__.py` `main` | Diagnostics only; never compared. |\n| Persistence, configuration, external stores | None | The product has no database or configuration. |\n\n## Technical Decisions\n\n- Exit codes: `0` success (including a report with no matching events), `1` operational failure,\n  `2` usage error.\n- Magnitudes are held as `decimal.Decimal` built from `str(value)` so that half-up rounding is exact.\n- CSV is written with Python's `csv` module, `lineterminator=\"\\n\"`, and encoded as UTF-8.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or the snapshot and never embeds a report row,\n  count, or distance.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC foundation-imports ===\nIntent: The cli package publishes main, the testing runner, and the two error types.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nimport cli\nfrom cli import main\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure, UsageError\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nassert callable(main)\nassert callable(cli_runner)\nassert issubclass(UsageError, Exception)\nassert issubclass(OperationalFailure, Exception)\nassert UsageError is not OperationalFailure\nassert sys.version_info >= (3, 11)\n=== END AC foundation-imports ===\n\n=== AC foundation-runner-contract ===\nIntent: cli_runner returns an integer exit code with text standard output and standard error without spawning a process.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner()\nprint(code, repr(out), repr(err))\nassert isinstance(code, int)\nassert isinstance(out, str)\nassert isinstance(err, str)\n=== END AC foundation-runner-contract ===\n\n=== AC foundation-executable ===\nIntent: The quakes file at the application root is executable and exits with the same code as cli.main.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nassert os.path.isfile(\"quakes\")\nassert os.access(\"quakes\", os.X_OK)\nwith open(\"quakes\", \"rb\") as handle:\n    first_two = handle.read(2)\nassert first_two == b\"#!\"\n\ninproc_code, _, _ = cli_runner()\nresult = subprocess.run([sys.executable, \"quakes\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\nprint(result.stdout)\nprint(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)\nassert result.returncode == inproc_code\n=== END AC foundation-executable ===\n\n=== AC foundation-pytest-fixture ===\nIntent: The root conftest exposes the cli_runner fixture and the project declares its dependency manifest.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nimport conftest\n\nassert hasattr(conftest, \"cli_runner\")\nassert os.path.isfile(\"pyproject.toml\")\nassert os.path.isdir(\"cli\")\n=== END AC foundation-pytest-fixture ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Do not modify, rewrite, regenerate, or substitute any file under `sources/`.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or the snapshot and never hardcodes a report row, a count, or a distance.\n- Standard library only; Python 3.11 or newer.\n- Diagnostics go to standard error and are never compared.\n- No test opens a network connection.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-CliDispatch.md ===\n# FEATURE: Cli Dispatch\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Parse the command and its options in any order with the file last, and dispatch to the registered command handler. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md |\n| Provides    | quakes <command> dispatch, cli.options.parse_args, cli.options.COMMANDS, cli.options.Invocation, cli.commands.HANDLERS, cli.commands.dispatch |\n| Consumes    | cli.main, cli.errors.UsageError, cli.errors.OperationalFailure |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes <command> [options] [<file>]`. The command comes first, options follow in any order, and\nthe file is last. Any malformed command line is a usage error. This feature parses and validates the\nshape of the command line and routes a parsed invocation to a handler; reports, validation of `near`\nranges, and exit-code mapping belong to other features.\n\n## Trigger\n\nEvery invocation of `quakes`.\n\n## Interface\n\n- `cli.options.COMMANDS`: tuple `(\"fetch\", \"summary\", \"top\", \"daily\", \"regions\", \"near\")`.\n- `cli.options.Invocation`: frozen dataclass with `command: str`, `options: dict[str, str]`, and\n  `file: str | None`. `options` is keyed by the option name without its leading `--` (`min-mag`,\n  `n`, `lat`, `lon`, `radius`, `start`, `end`, `out`) and holds the value text exactly as given.\n  An option that was not given is absent from the dict; the owning command applies defaults\n  (`n` = 10, fetch `min-mag` = 2.5).\n- `cli.options.parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> Invocation`, raising `cli.errors.UsageError`.\n- `cli.commands.HANDLERS`: plain `dict[str, Callable[[Invocation], str]]`; each handler returns the\n  complete standard-output text.\n- `cli.commands.dispatch(invocation) -> str`: calls `HANDLERS[invocation.command]`; when no handler is\n  registered it raises `cli.errors.OperationalFailure`.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. `argv[0]` is the command; an unknown command or an empty `argv` is a usage error.\n2. The token after an option name is always that option's value, even when it begins with `-`\n   (so `--lat -5.25` is valid). A missing value is a usage error.\n3. Options accepted per command:\n\n   | Command | Options | Positional file |\n   |---|---|---|\n   | `fetch` | `--start`, `--end`, `--out` (all required), `--min-mag` | none (an extra positional is a usage error) |\n   | `summary`, `daily`, `regions` | `--min-mag` | exactly one, last |\n   | `top` | `--min-mag`, `--n` | exactly one, last |\n   | `near` | `--lat`, `--lon`, `--radius`, `--min-mag` | exactly one, last |\n\n4. Any other option, or an option the command does not list, is a usage error.\n5. An option given more than once is a usage error.\n6. `--min-mag`, `--lat`, `--lon` and `--radius` values must match `-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?`. `--n` must be\n   a positive integer (`0`, negatives, decimals and text are usage errors). `--start` and `--end`\n   must have the shape `YYYY-MM-DD`.\n7. A report command with no file, or with more than one file, is a usage error.\n8. For `near`, the presence of `--lat`, `--lon`, `--radius` and the range checks belong to\n   FEATURE-NearValidation.md; the parser only accepts them.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC dispatch-option-order ===\nIntent: Options may appear in any order and parse to the same invocation with the file last.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nmag = \"5.5\"\ncount = \"3\"\nfirst = parse_args([\"top\", \"--min-mag\", mag, \"--n\", count, path])\nsecond = parse_args([\"top\", \"--n\", count, \"--min-mag\", mag, path])\nassert first.command == \"top\"\nassert first.options == second.options\nassert first.options[\"min-mag\"] == mag\nassert first.options[\"n\"] == count\nassert first.file == path\nassert second.file == path\n=== END AC dispatch-option-order ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-negative-values ===\nIntent: A value beginning with a minus sign is read as the option's value, not as an option.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nlat = \"-5.25\"\nlon = \"-170\"\nradius = \"100\"\ninv = parse_args([\"near\", \"--lat\", lat, \"--lon\", lon, \"--radius\", radius, path])\nassert inv.command == \"near\"\nassert inv.options[\"lat\"] == lat\nassert inv.options[\"lon\"] == lon\nassert inv.options[\"radius\"] == radius\nassert inv.file == path\n=== END AC dispatch-negative-values ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-every-command-parses ===\nIntent: Each report command parses with a file, and fetch parses with its required options and no file.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.options import COMMANDS, parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nstart = \"2025-01-01\"\nend = \"2025-01-08\"\nout = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"out.geojson\")\nfor command in (\"summary\", \"daily\", \"regions\", \"top\"):\n    assert command in COMMANDS\n    inv = parse_args([command, path])\n    assert inv.command == command\n    assert inv.file == path\nassert \"near\" in COMMANDS\nassert \"fetch\" in COMMANDS\nfetch = parse_args([\"fetch\", \"--end\", end, \"--start\", start, \"--out\", out, \"--min-mag\", \"4.5\"])\nassert fetch.command == \"fetch\"\nassert fetch.file is None\nassert fetch.options[\"start\"] == start\nassert fetch.options[\"end\"] == end\nassert fetch.options[\"out\"] == out\nassert fetch.options[\"min-mag\"] == \"4.5\"\nassert len(COMMANDS) == 6\n=== END AC dispatch-every-command-parses ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-usage-errors ===\nIntent: Every malformed command line raises UsageError.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nstart = \"2025-01-01\"\nend = \"2025-01-08\"\nout = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"out.geojson\")\nbad = [\n    [],\n    [\"frobnicate\", path],\n    [\"summary\"],\n    [\"summary\", path, path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--n\", \"3\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--bogus\", \"1\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"big\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \".5\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\"],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"5\", \"--min-mag\", \"6\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"0\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"-1\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"2.5\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"many\", path],\n    [\"daily\", \"--lat\", \"1\", path],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--end\", end],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--out\", out],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out, path],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"yesterday\", \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out],\n]\naccepted = []\nfor argv in bad:\n    try:\n        parse_args(list(argv))\n    except UsageError:\n        continue\n    accepted.append(argv)\nprint(f\"{len(bad) - len(accepted)} rejected, {len(accepted)} accepted\")\nassert accepted == []\n=== END AC dispatch-usage-errors ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-routes-to-handler ===\nIntent: dispatch calls the registered handler with the invocation and returns its text unchanged.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ntext = \"col_a,col_b\\nvalue,1\\n\"\nseen = []\n\ndef fake(invocation):\n    seen.append(invocation)\n    return text\n\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"summary\"] = fake\ninv = parse_args([\"summary\", path])\nassert commands.dispatch(inv) == text\nassert len(seen) == 1\nassert seen[0] is inv\n=== END AC dispatch-routes-to-handler ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-missing-handler ===\nIntent: Dispatching a command with no registered handler raises OperationalFailure.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ncommands.HANDLERS.pop(\"daily\", None)\ninv = parse_args([\"daily\", path])\ntry:\n    commands.dispatch(inv)\nexcept OperationalFailure:\n    pass\nelse:\n    raise AssertionError(\"dispatch of an unregistered command did not raise\")\n=== END AC dispatch-missing-handler ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- An option the command does not list is a usage error, never ignored.\n- The parser never opens the file; reading it belongs to the feed reader.\n- Handlers return text; only `main` writes to standard output.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-ExitCodes.md ===\n# FEATURE: Exit Codes\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Map outcomes to exit codes 0, 1 and 2 and guarantee empty standard output with one standard-error line on failure. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-CliDispatch.md |\n| Provides    | exit code contract |\n| Consumes    | quakes <command> dispatch, cli.errors.UsageError, cli.errors.OperationalFailure, cli.commands.dispatch |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`cli.main` turns the result of parsing and dispatching into a process exit code and guarantees that a\nfailing command writes nothing to standard output.\n\n## Rules\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `0` | Success, including a report with no matching events. The handler text is written to standard output exactly once. |\n| `1` | Operational failure (`OperationalFailure`): file unreadable or not a FeatureCollection; fetch network or HTTP failure. |\n| `2` | Usage error (`UsageError`): any malformed command line. |\n\n- `main` writes the handler's text to standard output only after the handler returned, so a failing\n  command has written nothing to standard output.\n- A failure writes exactly one diagnostic line to standard error (the exception message on a single\n  line, no traceback). Standard error is never compared.\n- `main` configures standard output as UTF-8 with `\\n` newlines when the stream supports\n  `reconfigure`, and writes the text without adding or altering line endings.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC exit-success-writes-text ===\nIntent: A handler that returns text yields exit 0 and exactly that text on standard output.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ntext = \"col_a,col_b\\nvalue,1\\n\"\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"summary\"] = lambda invocation: text\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"summary\", path)\nprint(code, repr(out), repr(err))\nassert code == 0\nassert out == text\n=== END AC exit-success-writes-text ===\n\n=== AC exit-empty-result-is-success ===\nIntent: A handler that returns no text still exits 0 with empty standard output.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"daily\"] = lambda invocation: \"\"\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"daily\", path)\nassert code == 0\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC exit-empty-result-is-success ===\n\n=== AC exit-operational-failure ===\nIntent: An OperationalFailure from a handler gives exit 1, empty standard output and a diagnostic on standard error.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\n\ndef failing(invocation):\n    raise OperationalFailure(\"cannot read the feed\")\n\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"regions\"] = failing\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", path)\nprint(code, repr(out), repr(err))\nassert code == 1\nassert out == \"\"\nassert err.strip() != \"\"\nassert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC exit-operational-failure ===\n\n=== AC exit-usage-error-from-handler ===\nIntent: A UsageError raised by a handler gives exit 2 and empty standard output.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\n\ndef rejecting(invocation):\n    raise UsageError(\"bad value\")\n\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"top\"] = rejecting\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"top\", path)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\nassert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC exit-usage-error-from-handler ===\n\n=== AC exit-parse-usage-errors ===\nIntent: Malformed command lines exit 2 with empty standard output and one diagnostic line.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ncases = [\n    [],\n    [\"frobnicate\", path],\n    [\"summary\"],\n    [\"summary\", \"--n\", \"3\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"big\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"0\", path],\n]\nbad = []\nfor argv in cases:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(*argv)\n    if code != 2 or out != \"\" or len(err.strip().splitlines()) != 1:\n        bad.append((argv, code, out, err))\nprint(bad)\nassert bad == []\n=== END AC exit-parse-usage-errors ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- A failing command never writes to standard output.\n- Standard error carries one diagnostic line and no traceback; it is never compared.\n- Exit code `0` is used for success including a report with no matching events.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Help.md ===\n# FEATURE: Help\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Provide help text for the program and for each command, shown by `--help`. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-CliDispatch.md |\n| Provides    | --help for quakes and each command, cli.help.wants_help, cli.help.help_text |\n| Consumes    | quakes <command> dispatch, cli.options.COMMANDS |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery command has help text so a user can discover its options. Help is requested output, not a\nfailure: it is written to standard output and exits `0` (decision Q-001).\n\n## Interface\n\n- `cli.help.help_text(command: str | None) -> str`: program-level help when `command` is `None`\n  (listing every command), otherwise that command's synopsis and options. Each command's text is\n  distinct.\n- `cli.help.wants_help(argv: list[str]) -> bool`: `True` when `argv[0]` is `--help`, or when\n  `argv[0]` is a known command and `--help` appears later in `argv`; otherwise `False`.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. `quakes --help` writes the program help and exits `0`.\n2. `quakes <command> --help` for each of `fetch`, `summary`, `top`, `daily`, `regions`, `near` writes\n   that command's help and exits `0`.\n3. Help is written before any file is read or any other validation is attempted.\n4. `quakes frobnicate --help` is not help: the unknown command is a usage error (exit `2`).\n5. `main` checks `wants_help` first, as step 2 of the control flow in ARCHITECTURE.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC help-program ===\nIntent: quakes --help prints program help to standard output and exits 0.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.help import help_text\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"--help\")\nprint(code, repr(err))\nassert code == 0\nassert out.strip() != \"\"\nassert out == help_text(None)\n=== END AC help-program ===\n\n=== AC help-every-command ===\nIntent: Every command has its own non-empty help text shown by --help with exit 0.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.help import help_text\nfrom cli.options import COMMANDS\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ntexts = {}\nfor command in COMMANDS:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(command, \"--help\")\n    print(command, code, repr(err))\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.strip() != \"\"\n    assert out == help_text(command)\n    texts[command] = out\nassert len(set(texts.values())) == len(COMMANDS)\nassert help_text(None) not in texts.values()\n=== END AC help-every-command ===\n\n=== AC help-wants-help ===\nIntent: wants_help recognises --help for the program and for known commands only.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.help import wants_help\nfrom cli.options import COMMANDS\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nassert wants_help([\"--help\"]) is True\nfor command in COMMANDS:\n    assert wants_help([command, \"--help\"]) is True\n    assert wants_help([command, \"--min-mag\", \"5\", \"--help\"]) is True\nassert wants_help([\"summary\", path]) is False\nassert wants_help([]) is False\n=== END AC help-wants-help ===\n\n=== AC help-unknown-command ===\nIntent: An unknown command with --help is a usage error, not help.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"frobnicate\", \"--help\")\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC help-unknown-command ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- Commander reads the help text for each command and finds the options listed in the instructions understandable.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Help never reads a file or touches the network.\n- `--help` is the only otherwise unlisted option that is accepted.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-FeedReader.md ===\n# FEATURE: Feed Reader\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Read a saved USGS GeoJSON FeatureCollection file into a list of events. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md |\n| Provides    | read_events(path), cli.reader.Event |\n| Consumes    | cli.errors.OperationalFailure |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`read_events` is the only function that reads a feed file. It turns the file into events, ignores\nevery field it does not need, and excludes events with no magnitude. Normalisation (time, region),\nfiltering and formatting are other functions.\n\n## Interface\n\n`cli.reader.Event` is a frozen dataclass:\n\n| Field | Type | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| `id` | `str` | feature `id` |\n| `mag` | `decimal.Decimal` | `Decimal(str(properties.mag))` |\n| `place` | `str \\| None` | `properties.place`, unchanged (`None` stays `None`) |\n| `time_ms` | `int` | `properties.time`, milliseconds since the Unix epoch |\n| `tsunami` | `int` | `properties.tsunami` (`1` or `0`) |\n| `lon` | `float` | `geometry.coordinates[0]` |\n| `lat` | `float` | `geometry.coordinates[1]` |\n| `depth_km` | `float` | `geometry.coordinates[2]` |\n\n`cli.reader.read_events(path: str | os.PathLike) -> list[Event]` returns events in file order.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. The file is read as UTF-8. A file that cannot be read, is not valid UTF-8, or is not JSON raises\n   `cli.errors.OperationalFailure`.\n2. The top level must be an object with `\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"` and a `features` array;\n   otherwise `OperationalFailure`.\n3. Every other field of a feature is ignored.\n4. A feature whose `properties.mag` is `null` is excluded.\n5. A feature that lacks a field the reader needs (other than a null `mag`, and a null `place` which is\n   kept as `None`) raises `OperationalFailure` rather than being skipped (decision Q-004).\n6. An empty `features` array yields an empty list.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC reader-fields ===\nIntent: read_events returns one Event per feature with the mapped fields, in file order, excluding null-magnitude features.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import Event, read_events\n\ndef feature(fid, mag, place, ms, tsunami, lon, lat, depth):\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"Feature\",\n        \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": ms, \"tsunami\": tsunami,\n                       \"updated\": 1, \"status\": \"reviewed\", \"sig\": 400},\n        \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [lon, lat, depth]},\n        \"id\": fid,\n    }\n\nfeatures = [\n    feature(\"ev-a\", 5.1, \"12 km N of Alpha, Beta\", 1735706358208, 0, 169.3819, -20.9273, 22),\n    feature(\"ev-null\", None, \"ignored\", 1735706358209, 0, 1.0, 2.0, 3),\n    feature(\"ev-b\", 7, None, 1736211916734, 1, 87.3781, 28.6036, 10.5),\n]\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"metadata\": {\"count\": 3}, \"features\": features}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"feed.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle)\n    events = read_events(path)\n\nexpected = [f for f in features if f[\"properties\"][\"mag\"] is not None]\nassert len(events) == len(expected)\nfor event, src in zip(events, expected):\n    assert isinstance(event, Event)\n    props = src[\"properties\"]\n    lon, lat, depth = src[\"geometry\"][\"coordinates\"]\n    assert event.id == src[\"id\"]\n    assert event.mag == Decimal(str(props[\"mag\"]))\n    assert event.place == props[\"place\"]\n    assert event.time_ms == props[\"time\"]\n    assert event.tsunami == props[\"tsunami\"]\n    assert event.lon == lon\n    assert event.lat == lat\n    assert event.depth_km == depth\n=== END AC reader-fields ===\n\n=== AC reader-empty-collection ===\nIntent: A FeatureCollection with an empty features array yields no events.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"empty.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle)\n    assert read_events(path) == []\n=== END AC reader-empty-collection ===\n\n=== AC reader-only-null-mag ===\nIntent: A collection whose only feature has a null magnitude yields no events.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\nfeature = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": None, \"place\": \"somewhere\", \"time\": 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]},\n    \"id\": \"only-null\",\n}\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [feature]}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"null.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle)\n    assert read_events(path) == []\n=== END AC reader-only-null-mag ===\n\n=== AC reader-operational-failures ===\nIntent: Unreadable, non-JSON, non-UTF-8, non-FeatureCollection, and malformed-feature files raise OperationalFailure.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\ngood_feature = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.0, \"place\": \"p\", \"time\": 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]},\n    \"id\": \"ok\",\n}\nno_geometry = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.0, \"place\": \"p\", \"time\": 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"id\": \"broken\",\n}\npayloads = {\n    \"not-json\": b\"this is not json\\n\",\n    \"not-utf8\": b\"\\xff\\xfe\\xfa\\xfb\",\n    \"single-feature\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"Feature\", \"properties\": {}, \"geometry\": None}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"no-features\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"features-not-list\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": {}}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"json-list\": json.dumps([good_feature]).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"missing-geometry\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [good_feature, no_geometry]}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n}\nsurvivors = []\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    for name, payload in payloads.items():\n        path = os.path.join(tmp, name + \".json\")\n        with open(path, \"wb\") as handle:\n            handle.write(payload)\n        try:\n            read_events(path)\n        except OperationalFailure:\n            continue\n        survivors.append(name)\n    try:\n        read_events(os.path.join(tmp, \"no-such-file.geojson\"))\n    except OperationalFailure:\n        pass\n    else:\n        survivors.append(\"no-such-file\")\nprint(survivors)\nassert survivors == []\n=== END AC reader-operational-failures ===\n\n=== AC reader-utf8-place ===\nIntent: Non-ASCII place text is read as UTF-8 and returned unchanged.\nEncoding: utf-8\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\nplace = \"13 km NW of \\u0100wash, Ethiopia\"\nfeature = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5, \"place\": place, \"time\": 1735718987701, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [40.0976, 9.0855, 10]},\n    \"id\": \"utf8-event\",\n}\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [feature]}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"utf8.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle, ensure_ascii=False)\n    events = read_events(path)\nassert len(events) == 1\nassert events[0].place == place\n=== END AC reader-utf8-place ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- The reader never reads `sources/run.sh` or the snapshot and embeds no event data.\n- Every field other than `id`, `mag`, `place`, `time`, `tsunami` and `geometry.coordinates` is ignored.\n- A failure to read the file never produces partial events.\n=== END ARTIFACT ==="}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":81326,"cache_read_input_tokens":1568,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":81326},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"50527b41-d0df-48df-ab1c-8690ba0e5b77","uuid":"c47a9558-d41a-4d30-a535-97486e90551d","timestamp":"2026-10-24T21:24:33.596Z","request_id":"req_011CgMmFNAADtuGjfduGsSdS"}

BEGIN ARTIFACT ARCHITECTURE.md ===\n# ARCHITECTURE: Quakes\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Module layout, boundaries and technical decisions for the `quakes` earthquake feed reporter command-line tool. |\n| Depends On  | None |\n| Provides    | quakes executable, cli.main, cli.testing.cli_runner, cli.errors.UsageError, cli.errors.OperationalFailure |\n| Consumes    | None |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes` is a Python 3.11+ standard-library command-line tool. `quakes fetch` saves a period of the\nUSGS FDSN event feed as a GeoJSON file. Five report commands (`summary`, `top`, `daily`, `regions`,\n`near`) read a saved file and write a CSV report to standard output. Every report value is computed\nfrom the file being read; nothing is embedded.\n\n## Technology Stack\n\nDerived from `TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md`, which remains the decision of record.\n\n| Technology | Where it applies |\n|---|---|\n| Python 3.11+ (standard library only) | All application code: `cli/` package and the `quakes` executable. |\n| CLI (`cli.md`) | The `quakes` entry point and the `cli` package with `main(argv) -> int`. |\n| pytest | The project test suite under `tests/`, run through `bin/test.sh`. |\n| USGS GeoJSON | Input format for every report; fetched with `urllib.request`. |\n| POSIX sh | `bin/test.sh` and the supplied grader `sources/run.sh`. |\n\n## Module Layout\n\nAll application code lives in the `cli` package at the application root.\n\n| Module | Responsibility | Built by story |\n|---|---|---|\n| `quakes` (root, executable) | `#!` Python launcher that calls `cli.main` and exits with its return value | foundation |\n| `cli/__init__.py` | `main(argv) -> int`: help check, parse, dispatch, exit-code mapping, writing stdout | foundation, then feature stories |\n| `cli/testing.py` | `cli_runner(*args) -> (exit_code, stdout, stderr)` | foundation |\n| `cli/errors.py` | `UsageError` and `OperationalFailure`, both `Exception` subclasses | foundation |\n| `cli/options.py` | `COMMANDS`, `Invocation`, `parse_args(argv)` | feature-cli-dispatch |\n| `cli/commands.py` | `HANDLERS` registry and `dispatch(invocation) -> str` | feature-cli-dispatch |\n| `cli/help.py` | `wants_help(argv)`, `help_text(command)` | feature-help |\n| `cli/reader.py` | `Event`, `read_events(path)` | feature-feed-reader |\n| `cli/normalise.py` | `format_time`, `region_of`, number formatting helpers | feature-event-normalise |\n| `cli/filtering.py` | `filter_min_mag(events, m)` | feature-min-mag |\n| `cli/reports.py` and per-report modules | One compute function and one format function per report | report stories |\n| `cli/fetch.py` | `http_get(url)` and the fetch handler | feature-fetch |\n\nReading the file, filtering, computing each report, and formatting are separate functions, each\nunit-tested on its own.\n\n## Control Flow\n\n`main(argv)` runs, in order:\n\n1. Reconfigure standard output to UTF-8 with `\\n` newlines when the stream supports it.\n2. If `cli.help.wants_help(argv)`, write the help text to standard output and return `0`.\n3. `invocation = parse_args(argv)`, then `text = commands.dispatch(invocation)`.\n4. Write `text` to standard output once, only after the handler has returned, and return `0`.\n5. `UsageError` returns `2` and `OperationalFailure` returns `1`. Each writes exactly one diagnostic\n   line to standard error and nothing to standard output.\n\nA handler is a function `handler(invocation) -> str` returning the complete standard-output text. A\nhandler never writes to standard output itself. This is what guarantees that a failing command\nwrites nothing to standard output.\n\n## Boundaries and Ownership\n\n| Boundary | Owning module | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Local file reads | `cli/reader.py` | The only module that opens a feed file for reading. |\n| Network | `cli/fetch.py` `http_get` | The only module that opens a connection; tests replace `http_get`. |\n| Standard output | `cli/__init__.py` `main` | Handlers return text. |\n| Standard error | `cli/__init__.py` `main` | Diagnostics only; never compared. |\n| Persistence, configuration, external stores | None | The product has no database or configuration. |\n\n## Technical Decisions\n\n- Exit codes: `0` success (including a report with no matching events), `1` operational failure,\n  `2` usage error.\n- Magnitudes are held as `decimal.Decimal` built from `str(value)` so that half-up rounding is exact.\n- CSV is written with Python's `csv` module, `lineterminator=\"\\n\"`, and encoded as UTF-8.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or the snapshot and never embeds a report row,\n  count, or distance.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC foundation-imports ===\nIntent: The cli package publishes main, the testing runner, and the two error types.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nimport cli\nfrom cli import main\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure, UsageError\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nassert callable(main)\nassert callable(cli_runner)\nassert issubclass(UsageError, Exception)\nassert issubclass(OperationalFailure, Exception)\nassert UsageError is not OperationalFailure\nassert sys.version_info >= (3, 11)\n=== END AC foundation-imports ===\n\n=== AC foundation-runner-contract ===\nIntent: cli_runner returns an integer exit code with text standard output and standard error without spawning a process.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner()\nprint(code, repr(out), repr(err))\nassert isinstance(code, int)\nassert isinstance(out, str)\nassert isinstance(err, str)\n=== END AC foundation-runner-contract ===\n\n=== AC foundation-executable ===\nIntent: The quakes file at the application root is executable and exits with the same code as cli.main.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nassert os.path.isfile(\"quakes\")\nassert os.access(\"quakes\", os.X_OK)\nwith open(\"quakes\", \"rb\") as handle:\n    first_two = handle.read(2)\nassert first_two == b\"#!\"\n\ninproc_code, _, _ = cli_runner()\nresult = subprocess.run([sys.executable, \"quakes\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\nprint(result.stdout)\nprint(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)\nassert result.returncode == inproc_code\n=== END AC foundation-executable ===\n\n=== AC foundation-pytest-fixture ===\nIntent: The root conftest exposes the cli_runner fixture and the project declares its dependency manifest.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nimport conftest\n\nassert hasattr(conftest, \"cli_runner\")\nassert os.path.isfile(\"pyproject.toml\")\nassert os.path.isdir(\"cli\")\n=== END AC foundation-pytest-fixture ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Do not modify, rewrite, regenerate, or substitute any file under `sources/`.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or the snapshot and never hardcodes a report row, a count, or a distance.\n- Standard library only; Python 3.11 or newer.\n- Diagnostics go to standard error and are never compared.\n- No test opens a network connection.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-CliDispatch.md ===\n# FEATURE: Cli Dispatch\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Parse the command and its options in any order with the file last, and dispatch to the registered command handler. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md |\n| Provides    | quakes <command> dispatch, cli.options.parse_args, cli.options.COMMANDS, cli.options.Invocation, cli.commands.HANDLERS, cli.commands.dispatch |\n| Consumes    | cli.main, cli.errors.UsageError, cli.errors.OperationalFailure |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes <command> [options] [<file>]`. The command comes first, options follow in any order, and\nthe file is last. Any malformed command line is a usage error. This feature parses and validates the\nshape of the command line and routes a parsed invocation to a handler; reports, validation of `near`\nranges, and exit-code mapping belong to other features.\n\n## Trigger\n\nEvery invocation of `quakes`.\n\n## Interface\n\n- `cli.options.COMMANDS`: tuple `(\"fetch\", \"summary\", \"top\", \"daily\", \"regions\", \"near\")`.\n- `cli.options.Invocation`: frozen dataclass with `command: str`, `options: dict[str, str]`, and\n  `file: str | None`. `options` is keyed by the option name without its leading `--` (`min-mag`,\n  `n`, `lat`, `lon`, `radius`, `start`, `end`, `out`) and holds the value text exactly as given.\n  An option that was not given is absent from the dict; the owning command applies defaults\n  (`n` = 10, fetch `min-mag` = 2.5).\n- `cli.options.parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> Invocation`, raising `cli.errors.UsageError`.\n- `cli.commands.HANDLERS`: plain `dict[str, Callable[[Invocation], str]]`; each handler returns the\n  complete standard-output text.\n- `cli.commands.dispatch(invocation) -> str`: calls `HANDLERS[invocation.command]`; when no handler is\n  registered it raises `cli.errors.OperationalFailure`.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. `argv[0]` is the command; an unknown command or an empty `argv` is a usage error.\n2. The token after an option name is always that option's value, even when it begins with `-`\n   (so `--lat -5.25` is valid). A missing value is a usage error.\n3. Options accepted per command:\n\n   | Command | Options | Positional file |\n   |---|---|---|\n   | `fetch` | `--start`, `--end`, `--out` (all required), `--min-mag` | none (an extra positional is a usage error) |\n   | `summary`, `daily`, `regions` | `--min-mag` | exactly one, last |\n   | `top` | `--min-mag`, `--n` | exactly one, last |\n   | `near` | `--lat`, `--lon`, `--radius`, `--min-mag` | exactly one, last |\n\n4. Any other option, or an option the command does not list, is a usage error.\n5. An option given more than once is a usage error.\n6. `--min-mag`, `--lat`, `--lon` and `--radius` values must match `-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?`. `--n` must be\n   a positive integer (`0`, negatives, decimals and text are usage errors). `--start` and `--end`\n   must have the shape `YYYY-MM-DD`.\n7. A report command with no file, or with more than one file, is a usage error.\n8. For `near`, the presence of `--lat`, `--lon`, `--radius` and the range checks belong to\n   FEATURE-NearValidation.md; the parser only accepts them.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC dispatch-option-order ===\nIntent: Options may appear in any order and parse to the same invocation with the file last.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nmag = \"5.5\"\ncount = \"3\"\nfirst = parse_args([\"top\", \"--min-mag\", mag, \"--n\", count, path])\nsecond = parse_args([\"top\", \"--n\", count, \"--min-mag\", mag, path])\nassert first.command == \"top\"\nassert first.options == second.options\nassert first.options[\"min-mag\"] == mag\nassert first.options[\"n\"] == count\nassert first.file == path\nassert second.file == path\n=== END AC dispatch-option-order ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-negative-values ===\nIntent: A value beginning with a minus sign is read as the option's value, not as an option.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nlat = \"-5.25\"\nlon = \"-170\"\nradius = \"100\"\ninv = parse_args([\"near\", \"--lat\", lat, \"--lon\", lon, \"--radius\", radius, path])\nassert inv.command == \"near\"\nassert inv.options[\"lat\"] == lat\nassert inv.options[\"lon\"] == lon\nassert inv.options[\"radius\"] == radius\nassert inv.file == path\n=== END AC dispatch-negative-values ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-every-command-parses ===\nIntent: Each report command parses with a file, and fetch parses with its required options and no file.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.options import COMMANDS, parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nstart = \"2025-01-01\"\nend = \"2025-01-08\"\nout = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"out.geojson\")\nfor command in (\"summary\", \"daily\", \"regions\", \"top\"):\n    assert command in COMMANDS\n    inv = parse_args([command, path])\n    assert inv.command == command\n    assert inv.file == path\nassert \"near\" in COMMANDS\nassert \"fetch\" in COMMANDS\nfetch = parse_args([\"fetch\", \"--end\", end, \"--start\", start, \"--out\", out, \"--min-mag\", \"4.5\"])\nassert fetch.command == \"fetch\"\nassert fetch.file is None\nassert fetch.options[\"start\"] == start\nassert fetch.options[\"end\"] == end\nassert fetch.options[\"out\"] == out\nassert fetch.options[\"min-mag\"] == \"4.5\"\nassert len(COMMANDS) == 6\n=== END AC dispatch-every-command-parses ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-usage-errors ===\nIntent: Every malformed command line raises UsageError.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nstart = \"2025-01-01\"\nend = \"2025-01-08\"\nout = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"out.geojson\")\nbad = [\n    [],\n    [\"frobnicate\", path],\n    [\"summary\"],\n    [\"summary\", path, path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--n\", \"3\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--bogus\", \"1\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"big\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \".5\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\"],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"5\", \"--min-mag\", \"6\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"0\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"-1\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"2.5\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"many\", path],\n    [\"daily\", \"--lat\", \"1\", path],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--end\", end],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--out\", out],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out, path],\n    [\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"yesterday\", \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out],\n]\naccepted = []\nfor argv in bad:\n    try:\n        parse_args(list(argv))\n    except UsageError:\n        continue\n    accepted.append(argv)\nprint(f\"{len(bad) - len(accepted)} rejected, {len(accepted)} accepted\")\nassert accepted == []\n=== END AC dispatch-usage-errors ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-routes-to-handler ===\nIntent: dispatch calls the registered handler with the invocation and returns its text unchanged.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ntext = \"col_a,col_b\\nvalue,1\\n\"\nseen = []\n\ndef fake(invocation):\n    seen.append(invocation)\n    return text\n\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"summary\"] = fake\ninv = parse_args([\"summary\", path])\nassert commands.dispatch(inv) == text\nassert len(seen) == 1\nassert seen[0] is inv\n=== END AC dispatch-routes-to-handler ===\n\n=== AC dispatch-missing-handler ===\nIntent: Dispatching a command with no registered handler raises OperationalFailure.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure\nfrom cli.options import parse_args\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ncommands.HANDLERS.pop(\"daily\", None)\ninv = parse_args([\"daily\", path])\ntry:\n    commands.dispatch(inv)\nexcept OperationalFailure:\n    pass\nelse:\n    raise AssertionError(\"dispatch of an unregistered command did not raise\")\n=== END AC dispatch-missing-handler ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- An option the command does not list is a usage error, never ignored.\n- The parser never opens the file; reading it belongs to the feed reader.\n- Handlers return text; only `main` writes to standard output.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-ExitCodes.md ===\n# FEATURE: Exit Codes\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Map outcomes to exit codes 0, 1 and 2 and guarantee empty standard output with one standard-error line on failure. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-CliDispatch.md |\n| Provides    | exit code contract |\n| Consumes    | quakes <command> dispatch, cli.errors.UsageError, cli.errors.OperationalFailure, cli.commands.dispatch |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`cli.main` turns the result of parsing and dispatching into a process exit code and guarantees that a\nfailing command writes nothing to standard output.\n\n## Rules\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `0` | Success, including a report with no matching events. The handler text is written to standard output exactly once. |\n| `1` | Operational failure (`OperationalFailure`): file unreadable or not a FeatureCollection; fetch network or HTTP failure. |\n| `2` | Usage error (`UsageError`): any malformed command line. |\n\n- `main` writes the handler's text to standard output only after the handler returned, so a failing\n  command has written nothing to standard output.\n- A failure writes exactly one diagnostic line to standard error (the exception message on a single\n  line, no traceback). Standard error is never compared.\n- `main` configures standard output as UTF-8 with `\\n` newlines when the stream supports\n  `reconfigure`, and writes the text without adding or altering line endings.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC exit-success-writes-text ===\nIntent: A handler that returns text yields exit 0 and exactly that text on standard output.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ntext = \"col_a,col_b\\nvalue,1\\n\"\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"summary\"] = lambda invocation: text\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"summary\", path)\nprint(code, repr(out), repr(err))\nassert code == 0\nassert out == text\n=== END AC exit-success-writes-text ===\n\n=== AC exit-empty-result-is-success ===\nIntent: A handler that returns no text still exits 0 with empty standard output.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"daily\"] = lambda invocation: \"\"\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"daily\", path)\nassert code == 0\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC exit-empty-result-is-success ===\n\n=== AC exit-operational-failure ===\nIntent: An OperationalFailure from a handler gives exit 1, empty standard output and a diagnostic on standard error.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\n\ndef failing(invocation):\n    raise OperationalFailure(\"cannot read the feed\")\n\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"regions\"] = failing\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", path)\nprint(code, repr(out), repr(err))\nassert code == 1\nassert out == \"\"\nassert err.strip() != \"\"\nassert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC exit-operational-failure ===\n\n=== AC exit-usage-error-from-handler ===\nIntent: A UsageError raised by a handler gives exit 2 and empty standard output.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli import commands\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\n\ndef rejecting(invocation):\n    raise UsageError(\"bad value\")\n\ncommands.HANDLERS[\"top\"] = rejecting\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"top\", path)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\nassert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC exit-usage-error-from-handler ===\n\n=== AC exit-parse-usage-errors ===\nIntent: Malformed command lines exit 2 with empty standard output and one diagnostic line.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\ncases = [\n    [],\n    [\"frobnicate\", path],\n    [\"summary\"],\n    [\"summary\", \"--n\", \"3\", path],\n    [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"big\", path],\n    [\"top\", \"--n\", \"0\", path],\n]\nbad = []\nfor argv in cases:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(*argv)\n    if code != 2 or out != \"\" or len(err.strip().splitlines()) != 1:\n        bad.append((argv, code, out, err))\nprint(bad)\nassert bad == []\n=== END AC exit-parse-usage-errors ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- A failing command never writes to standard output.\n- Standard error carries one diagnostic line and no traceback; it is never compared.\n- Exit code `0` is used for success including a report with no matching events.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Help.md ===\n# FEATURE: Help\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Provide help text for the program and for each command, shown by `--help`. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-CliDispatch.md |\n| Provides    | --help for quakes and each command, cli.help.wants_help, cli.help.help_text |\n| Consumes    | quakes <command> dispatch, cli.options.COMMANDS |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery command has help text so a user can discover its options. Help is requested output, not a\nfailure: it is written to standard output and exits `0` (decision Q-001).\n\n## Interface\n\n- `cli.help.help_text(command: str | None) -> str`: program-level help when `command` is `None`\n  (listing every command), otherwise that command's synopsis and options. Each command's text is\n  distinct.\n- `cli.help.wants_help(argv: list[str]) -> bool`: `True` when `argv[0]` is `--help`, or when\n  `argv[0]` is a known command and `--help` appears later in `argv`; otherwise `False`.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. `quakes --help` writes the program help and exits `0`.\n2. `quakes <command> --help` for each of `fetch`, `summary`, `top`, `daily`, `regions`, `near` writes\n   that command's help and exits `0`.\n3. Help is written before any file is read or any other validation is attempted.\n4. `quakes frobnicate --help` is not help: the unknown command is a usage error (exit `2`).\n5. `main` checks `wants_help` first, as step 2 of the control flow in ARCHITECTURE.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC help-program ===\nIntent: quakes --help prints program help to standard output and exits 0.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.help import help_text\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"--help\")\nprint(code, repr(err))\nassert code == 0\nassert out.strip() != \"\"\nassert out == help_text(None)\n=== END AC help-program ===\n\n=== AC help-every-command ===\nIntent: Every command has its own non-empty help text shown by --help with exit 0.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.help import help_text\nfrom cli.options import COMMANDS\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ntexts = {}\nfor command in COMMANDS:\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(command, \"--help\")\n    print(command, code, repr(err))\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.strip() != \"\"\n    assert out == help_text(command)\n    texts[command] = out\nassert len(set(texts.values())) == len(COMMANDS)\nassert help_text(None) not in texts.values()\n=== END AC help-every-command ===\n\n=== AC help-wants-help ===\nIntent: wants_help recognises --help for the program and for known commands only.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.help import wants_help\nfrom cli.options import COMMANDS\n\npath = os.path.join(\"somewhere\", \"feed.geojson\")\nassert wants_help([\"--help\"]) is True\nfor command in COMMANDS:\n    assert wants_help([command, \"--help\"]) is True\n    assert wants_help([command, \"--min-mag\", \"5\", \"--help\"]) is True\nassert wants_help([\"summary\", path]) is False\nassert wants_help([]) is False\n=== END AC help-wants-help ===\n\n=== AC help-unknown-command ===\nIntent: An unknown command with --help is a usage error, not help.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"frobnicate\", \"--help\")\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC help-unknown-command ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- Commander reads the help text for each command and finds the options listed in the instructions understandable.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Help never reads a file or touches the network.\n- `--help` is the only otherwise unlisted option that is accepted.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-FeedReader.md ===\n# FEATURE: Feed Reader\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | Read a saved USGS GeoJSON FeatureCollection file into a list of events. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md |\n| Provides    | read_events(path), cli.reader.Event |\n| Consumes    | cli.errors.OperationalFailure |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`read_events` is the only function that reads a feed file. It turns the file into events, ignores\nevery field it does not need, and excludes events with no magnitude. Normalisation (time, region),\nfiltering and formatting are other functions.\n\n## Interface\n\n`cli.reader.Event` is a frozen dataclass:\n\n| Field | Type | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| `id` | `str` | feature `id` |\n| `mag` | `decimal.Decimal` | `Decimal(str(properties.mag))` |\n| `place` | `str \\| None` | `properties.place`, unchanged (`None` stays `None`) |\n| `time_ms` | `int` | `properties.time`, milliseconds since the Unix epoch |\n| `tsunami` | `int` | `properties.tsunami` (`1` or `0`) |\n| `lon` | `float` | `geometry.coordinates[0]` |\n| `lat` | `float` | `geometry.coordinates[1]` |\n| `depth_km` | `float` | `geometry.coordinates[2]` |\n\n`cli.reader.read_events(path: str | os.PathLike) -> list[Event]` returns events in file order.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. The file is read as UTF-8. A file that cannot be read, is not valid UTF-8, or is not JSON raises\n   `cli.errors.OperationalFailure`.\n2. The top level must be an object with `\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"` and a `features` array;\n   otherwise `OperationalFailure`.\n3. Every other field of a feature is ignored.\n4. A feature whose `properties.mag` is `null` is excluded.\n5. A feature that lacks a field the reader needs (other than a null `mag`, and a null `place` which is\n   kept as `None`) raises `OperationalFailure` rather than being skipped (decision Q-004).\n6. An empty `features` array yields an empty list.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC reader-fields ===\nIntent: read_events returns one Event per feature with the mapped fields, in file order, excluding null-magnitude features.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import Event, read_events\n\ndef feature(fid, mag, place, ms, tsunami, lon, lat, depth):\n    return {\n        \"type\": \"Feature\",\n        \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": ms, \"tsunami\": tsunami,\n                       \"updated\": 1, \"status\": \"reviewed\", \"sig\": 400},\n        \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [lon, lat, depth]},\n        \"id\": fid,\n    }\n\nfeatures = [\n    feature(\"ev-a\", 5.1, \"12 km N of Alpha, Beta\", 1735706358208, 0, 169.3819, -20.9273, 22),\n    feature(\"ev-null\", None, \"ignored\", 1735706358209, 0, 1.0, 2.0, 3),\n    feature(\"ev-b\", 7, None, 1736211916734, 1, 87.3781, 28.6036, 10.5),\n]\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"metadata\": {\"count\": 3}, \"features\": features}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"feed.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle)\n    events = read_events(path)\n\nexpected = [f for f in features if f[\"properties\"][\"mag\"] is not None]\nassert len(events) == len(expected)\nfor event, src in zip(events, expected):\n    assert isinstance(event, Event)\n    props = src[\"properties\"]\n    lon, lat, depth = src[\"geometry\"][\"coordinates\"]\n    assert event.id == src[\"id\"]\n    assert event.mag == Decimal(str(props[\"mag\"]))\n    assert event.place == props[\"place\"]\n    assert event.time_ms == props[\"time\"]\n    assert event.tsunami == props[\"tsunami\"]\n    assert event.lon == lon\n    assert event.lat == lat\n    assert event.depth_km == depth\n=== END AC reader-fields ===\n\n=== AC reader-empty-collection ===\nIntent: A FeatureCollection with an empty features array yields no events.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"empty.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle)\n    assert read_events(path) == []\n=== END AC reader-empty-collection ===\n\n=== AC reader-only-null-mag ===\nIntent: A collection whose only feature has a null magnitude yields no events.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\nfeature = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": None, \"place\": \"somewhere\", \"time\": 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]},\n    \"id\": \"only-null\",\n}\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [feature]}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"null.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle)\n    assert read_events(path) == []\n=== END AC reader-only-null-mag ===\n\n=== AC reader-operational-failures ===\nIntent: Unreadable, non-JSON, non-UTF-8, non-FeatureCollection, and malformed-feature files raise OperationalFailure.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalFailure\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\ngood_feature = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.0, \"place\": \"p\", \"time\": 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]},\n    \"id\": \"ok\",\n}\nno_geometry = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.0, \"place\": \"p\", \"time\": 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"id\": \"broken\",\n}\npayloads = {\n    \"not-json\": b\"this is not json\\n\",\n    \"not-utf8\": b\"\\xff\\xfe\\xfa\\xfb\",\n    \"single-feature\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"Feature\", \"properties\": {}, \"geometry\": None}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"no-features\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\"}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"features-not-list\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": {}}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"json-list\": json.dumps([good_feature]).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n    \"missing-geometry\": json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [good_feature, no_geometry]}).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n}\nsurvivors = []\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    for name, payload in payloads.items():\n        path = os.path.join(tmp, name + \".json\")\n        with open(path, \"wb\") as handle:\n            handle.write(payload)\n        try:\n            read_events(path)\n        except OperationalFailure:\n            continue\n        survivors.append(name)\n    try:\n        read_events(os.path.join(tmp, \"no-such-file.geojson\"))\n    except OperationalFailure:\n        pass\n    else:\n        survivors.append(\"no-such-file\")\nprint(survivors)\nassert survivors == []\n=== END AC reader-operational-failures ===\n\n=== AC reader-utf8-place ===\nIntent: Non-ASCII place text is read as UTF-8 and returned unchanged.\nEncoding: utf-8\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n\nfrom cli.reader import read_events\n\nplace = \"13 km NW of \\u0100wash, Ethiopia\"\nfeature = {\n    \"type\": \"Feature\",\n    \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5, \"place\": place, \"time\": 1735718987701, \"tsunami\": 0},\n    \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [40.0976, 9.0855, 10]},\n    \"id\": \"utf8-event\",\n}\ndoc = {\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [feature]}\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"utf8.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        json.dump(doc, handle, ensure_ascii=False)\n    events = read_events(path)\nassert len(events) == 1\nassert events[0].place == place\n=== END AC reader-utf8-place ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- The reader never reads `sources/run.sh` or the snapshot and embeds no event data.\n- Every field other than `id`, `mag`, `place`, `time`, `tsunami` and `geometry.coordinates` is ignored.\n- A failure to read the file never produces partial events.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===","ttft_ms":84062,"type":"result","duration_ms":152428,"uuid":"a4a5dfd3-2d97-4131-9888-8c8fb656531c","ttft_stream_ms":2375,"time_to_request_ms":151,"first_content_frame_ms":2376,"queued_turn_count":0,"result_index":0,"model_usage_since_last_result":{"claude-sonnet-5-5":{"inputTokens":2,"outputTokens":23625,"cacheReadInputTokens":1568,"cacheCreationInputTokens":81326,"webSearchRequests":0,"costUSD":0.5617148000000001,"contextWindow":1000000,"maxOutputTokens":128000,"thinkingTokens":10276,"canonicalModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","provider":"firstParty","costBasis":"list"}}}
